 Order
Heard on I.A.No.4833/2025, which is an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay.

Delay of 77 days in filing the appeal is duly explained in the application, which is well supported by an affidavit, therefore, application is allowed for the reasons stated therein and delay in filing the appeal is hereby condoned.
Heard finally with the consent of the parties.

This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 26/11/2024 passed by Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Mandsaur (M.P.) in MACC No.362/2022, whereby an amount of Rs.47,328/- has been awarded from the date of filing of claim petition i.e. 20/10/2022 to the appellant / claimant with interest @
6% per annum.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:9049 2 MA-4361-2025 2.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that Disability Certificate (Ex.-P/96) reveals disablement of 20% and Dr. Sanjay Sharma (AW-6) has also been examined to prove the disability,
but learned Claims Tribunal has ignored the aforesaid evidence, therefore, prays for considering 4%
permanent disability to the proportion of whole body.
2.1

He further submits that income of the claimant is to be assessed on the basis of circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act by the Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh, according to Yashpalsingh Shaktawat vs Manoj Patel on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114706558/
1 which on the date of accident i.e. 09/05/2022 income of the injured comes to Rs.9,125/- per month considering him 'Unskilled Labour'.
2.2

sentences.text: Future prospects @ 40% is also to be added in the compensation amount as per para 59.4 of the National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 and considering the age 24 years of the appellant multiplier of 18 is to be adopted.

sentences.text: 2.3 Learned counsel further submits that learned Claims Tribunal has also committed an error in not awarding any amount in the head of Transportation, therefore, appropriate amount should be awarded in this head also.
On these contentions, learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the award amount as prayed for.
3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that evidence led before the learned Claims Tribunal has been rightly appreciated.
The amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.

All the factors have been considered by the learned Claims Tribunal while NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:9049 3 MA-4361-2025 awarding the compensation amount and no fault can be found with in the impugned award.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the appeal being devoid of any substance.

4. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5.

From perusal of the Disability Certificate (Ex.-P/96) it reveals that claimant has suffered 20%
permanent disability and Dr. Sanjay Sharma (PW- 6) has proved the disability certificate, therefore, 4% permanent disability should have been assessed to the whole proportion of the body.
6.

As per the circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act, on the date of accident the income of the claimant comes to Rs.9,125/- per month and as per para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi's case (Supra) ,
40% future prospects should have been given to the claimant.

Similarly, looking the age of claimant,
multiplier of 18 is adopted.
An amount of Rs.2,000/- is also added in the head of transportation.

7. Accordingly, the just and proper compensation amount comes as under:
4% PD Rs.1,10,376/-
 Permanent Disability: (Rs.9,125/- pm + 40% FP x 12 m  x Multiplier of 18 =Rs.27,59,4

Medical Expenses: Rs.4,076/-
 Loss of Income: Rs.18,252/- (for 2 months)
 Pain and Suffering: Rs.10,000/-
Special
Diet: Rs.5,000/-

Attendant Expenses: Rs.10,000/-
 Transportation: Rs.2,000/-

Yashpalsingh Shaktawat vs Manoj Patel on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114706558/
2

Total: Rs.1,59,704/-
 MACT Awarded: Rs.47,328/-
 Enhanced Amount: Rs.1,12,376/-
 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:9049  4
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.1,59,704/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.47,328/-.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of Rs.1,12,376/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
8. Resultantly, the appeal filed by the appellant / claimant is allowed to the extent as indicated hereinabove.

Other terms and conditions of the impugned award including rate of interest @ 6%
shall remain intact.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate.
(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Tej Yashpalsingh Shaktawat vs Manoj Patel on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114706558/
